_comment: Ratchet baseline for `npm run check:src-complexity-drift` (development/scripts/check-src-complexity-drift.ts), captured 2026-08-17 at HEAD f23f2d3b (`git rev-parse HEAD`). Measured by that script's own findViolations() -- fresh ESLint `complexity` + `sonarjs/cognitive-complexity` rules hard-overridden to `error`/9 via `--rule` (same tool and threshold as apps/admin's own hard gate, see admin-complexity-debt.json -- do NOT compare these counts to any other complexity number in this repo without checking both use the same tool/threshold/scope), scoped to `src/server/routes/**` ONLY (not all of `src/` -- see the checker's own header for why), excluding __tests__/__measurements__. 115 violations across 72 files at capture time -- moved twice already during this same session (the 2026-08-16 audit measured 113/70, an earlier capture this session measured 115/71) because 6+ other agents were actively editing this tree concurrently, exactly as the dispatch brief warned. Re-run `npx tsx development/scripts/check-src-complexity-drift.ts` against a fresh tree before trusting this file's count as current -- staleness here is expected, not a bug. `check:src-complexity-drift` fails ONLY on a violation not already listed here (matched as a MULTISET on (rule, file, reason) -- see the checker's header for why a plain Set is wrong: `admin/widgets/agent-tools.ts` genuinely carries two textually-identical `complexity` violations today), so the gate is real and enforced from day one on `src/server/routes` while the existing debt gets paid down on its own schedule. Delete an entry once its violation is fixed -- `check:src-complexity-drift` reports (without failing on) any entry here that no longer reproduces, as a prompt to do exactly that. Never add an entry to silence a NEW violation without fixing it first.
